title: Formal Divisibility Rules for Various Bases and Moduli
description: A comprehensive collection of formally verified divisibility rules: general last-k-digits framework, power-of-2/5 generalizations, truncation methods for 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19, casting out nines/threes, digital root theory, and coprime factorization rules.

overview.historicalContext:
Divisibility rules have been known since ancient times. This extension formalizes a comprehensive collection of such rules in Lean 4, going far beyond the basic divisibility-by-3 rule.

The rules fall into three families:
1. **Last-k-digits rules**: When d divides the base power (e.g., 4|100), check the last k digits
2. **Digit-sum rules**: When base ≡ 1 (mod d), check the digit sum
3. **Truncation rules**: Reduce the number by removing a digit and adjusting (e.g., for 7 and 13)

All three families are unified through modular arithmetic.
overview.problemStatement:
Formalize a comprehensive collection of divisibility rules:

**Last-k-digits (general)**: If $d | M$, then $d | n \iff d | (n \bmod M)$

**Digit-sum (general)**: If $b \equiv 1 \pmod{d}$, then $d | n \iff d | \text{(digits sum in base }b\text{)}$

**Truncation for 13**: $13 | n \iff 13 | (\lfloor n/10 \rfloor + 4 \cdot (n \bmod 10))$

**Coprime factorization**: If $\gcd(d_1, d_2) = 1$, then $d_1 d_2 | n \iff d_1 | n \wedge d_2 | n$

**Digital root**: $\text{dr}(n) = 9 \iff 9 | n$ (for $n > 0$); $3 | n \iff 3 | \text{dr}(n)$
overview.text: A comprehensive collection of formally verified divisibility rules: general last-k-digits framework, power-of-2/5 generalizations, truncation methods for 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19, casting out nines/threes, digital root theory, and coprime factorization rules.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proofs use three main techniques:

1. **Modular arithmetic**: The general last-k-digits theorem follows from n = M·q + r, so if d|M then d|n iff d|r.

2. **Mathlib's digit infrastructure**: Nat.modEq_digits_sum provides digit-sum congruences for any base-divisor pair where base ≡ 1 (mod d).

3. **Integer lifting for truncation**: The divisibility-by-13 proof works in ℤ, using the identity 10(q + 4r) = n + 39r, then extracting divisibility via coprimality of 13 and 10.
keyInsights: All last-k-digits rules are instances of one general theorem: d|M → (d|n ↔ d|(n%M))
Digit-sum rules work in any base b where b ≡ 1 (mod d), not just base 10
Truncation methods use a multiply-and-cancel trick: 10(q + cr) = n + (10c-1)r
Digital root is characterized by mod 9 arithmetic with special case for multiples of 9
Coprime factorization reduces composite divisibility to prime-power tests

sections.title: General Last-k-Digits Framework
sections.summary: Unified theorem for last-digit rules (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 5, 25, 125) including binary and hexadecimal bases.

sections.title: Power-of-2 and Power-of-5 Theorems
sections.summary: General theorems: 2^k | n ↔ 2^k | (n mod 10^k), and similarly for 5^k.

sections.title: Divisibility by 13 via Truncation
sections.summary: The 'add 4 times the last digit' rule for 13, proved via integer arithmetic and coprimality.

sections.title: Digit-Sum Rules in Various Bases
sections.summary: Instantiations of the general digit-sum rule for 37 (base 1000), 99 (base 100), 999, 27, and rules in hex, octal, and other bases.

sections.title: Casting Out Nines and Threes
sections.summary: Casting out nines/threes preserves addition and multiplication modulo 9/3.

sections.title: Digital Root Theory
sections.summary: Digital root definition, bound ≤ 9, positivity, divisibility-by-9 characterization, and mod-3 property.

sections.title: Coprime Factorization Rules
sections.summary: Rules for 6, 12, 15, 18, 36, 45, 60, 90 via coprime factor decomposition.

sections.title: Truncation Methods for 7 and 11
sections.summary: Divisibility by 7 via subtract-2x-last-digit and divisibility by 11 via subtract-last-digit, both proved via integer arithmetic and coprimality.

sections.title: Truncation Methods for 17 and 19
sections.summary: Divisibility by 17 via subtract-5x-last-digit and divisibility by 19 via add-2x-last-digit.

sections.title: Summary Theorem
sections.summary: Master summary combining digit-sum, last-digit, and power generalization rules.

conclusion.summary: This extension provides a comprehensive, formally verified collection of divisibility rules covering three major families: last-k-digits, digit-sum, and truncation methods. Truncation rules are proved for all primes up to 19 coprime to 10 (7, 11, 13, 17, 19). All 50+ theorems are proved without sorry or axiom, building on Mathlib's digit and modular arithmetic infrastructure.
conclusion.implications:
The proof demonstrates the power of unifying theorems:

**1. One theorem, many rules**: The general last-k-digits theorem (d|M → d|n ↔ d|(n%M)) instantly gives all power-of-2 and power-of-5 rules.

**2. Base-agnostic digit sums**: The digit-sum framework works in any base, giving rules for divisibility by 37, 99, 999, and more via base 1000/100.

**3. Digital root theory**: The complete characterization of digital root connects elementary arithmetic to modular algebra.

**4. Practical checking**: Casting out nines and coprime factorization provide verified foundations for mental arithmetic techniques.
openQuestions: Can the truncation method be generalized to a single parametric theorem for arbitrary primes?
How do these rules extend to divisibility in polynomial rings?
